newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN STATE NOTES? NEVER HEARD OF THEM - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN STATE NOTES? NEVER HEARD OF THEM - SURVEY.

text.p: Ask Belgians to name investment products and just 1.5 percent would think of state notes, the new high-profile product launched by the finance ministry Treasury in June, according to Credit Lyonnais Belgium (CLB).
This compares with 40.5 percent for the state notes' rival product, commercial bank savings certificates, a Censydiam market survey ordered by CLB, which is a unit of Credit Lyonnais, showed.
CLB said the survey of 455 people showed that 52.5 percent of the holders of savings certificates would be interested in subscribing for state notes, if only they were properly explained.

CLB said in a statement that commercial bank savings certificates, the country's most popular investment product, were the main financial asset for Belgians with a total market value of 3,600 billion francs.

It said this showed that the growth potential for the state notes -- if sufficient information was provided by the Treasury and distributing banks -- could amount to 1,800 billion francs in the medium term.
The first issue of the Belgian Treasury's new state notes programme to retail investors in June raised a total of 16.65 billion francs, which was below market expectations.
The finance ministry said earlier it aimed to raise around 85 billion francs through four issues in 12 months.

A second issue will be launched on September 18, with retail investors able to choose between a five-year note extendable to seven years -- with a fixed interest rate -- and the three-five-seven year note with revisable rates and a minimum guarantee.
